key_phenomenon_and_finding: Discovery of quasi-steady invisible cool flames (~700 K, ~500-800 K range) sustained by low-temperature oxidation chemistry (NTC regime) after radiative extinction of the hot flame; lower LOI than 1g
safety_implication: Visual hot-flame extinction does not guarantee fire safety; toxic CO and formaldehyde (CH2O) persist; requires higher inert suppressant concentrations
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS Destiny Lab CIR (Combustion Integrated Rack) with MDCA (Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus) chamber insert for isolated free-floating or tethered droplets
principal_investigators: Forman A. Williams (PI, UC San Diego); Co-Is: Frederick L. Dryer (Princeton), Daniel L. Dietrich (NASA GRC), Vedha Nayagam (CWRU/NASA GRC)
scientific_link_and_applications: Baseline microgravity droplet data isolating NTC/cool-flame kinetics from buoyancy; directly validates chemical mechanisms for high-efficiency low-soot IC engines (HCCI, RCCI, LTC) and inspired ACME radiative extinction and gaseous cool-flame studies
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA/TP-2015-216046; PSI: FLEX; Nayagam, Dietrich, Ferkul, Hicks & Williams (2012), Combustion and Flame 159(12), 3583-3588

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Extended FLEX to heavier alkanes, multi-component mixtures, and twin droplets; discovered two-stage combustion, cool-flame reignition back to hot flame, and oscillating warm flames at high pressure
safety_implication: Risk of delayed hot-flame reignition from a persistent cool flame if compartment pressure rises or fresh O2 enters
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS CIR / MDCA upgraded with multi-component fuel dispensing, twin-droplet deployment, and higher-pressure/higher-O2 testing (including Cool Flames Investigation - CFI)
principal_investigators: Forman A. Williams (PI, UC San Diego); Co-Is: Frederick L. Dryer, Daniel L. Dietrich, Vedha Nayagam, Paul V. Ferkul
scientific_link_and_applications: Bridges single-component alkane kinetics to real multi-component transportation/aviation fuels and LTC/HCCI autoignition dynamics; directly motivated ACME CFI-G for gaseous cool flames
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: FLEX-2 / CFI; NASA Task Book / ISS Research Explorer: Flame Extinguishment Experiment-2 (FLEX-2)

fuel.material: SIBAL (75% cotton/25% fiberglass), PMMA, Nomex, Ultem, FR cotton

key_phenomenon_and_finding: U-shaped flammability boundary in 0g: absence of 1g buoyant convection (~20-30 cm/s) reduces convective cooling/blow-off at low forced flows (1-10 cm/s), creating thicker boundary layers until radiative quenching below 1-2 cm/s; SIBAL burned at 13.6% O2 (-2.4% safety margin vs 1g)
safety_implication: Earth upward flame-spread certification NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not always conservative in low-flow spacecraft HVAC regimes; restarting airflow causes rapid flare-up
hardware_and_rack_details: MSG (Microgravity Science Glovebox) housing modified SPICE (Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment) small wind-tunnel duct with solid sample holders
principal_investigators: Sandra L. Olson (PI, NASA GRC); Fletcher J. Miller (PI, San Diego State Univ.)
scientific_link_and_applications: Demonstrates that radiative vs convective heat-loss balance in 0g governs solid flammability; complements ACME BRE (gaseous emulation of solid burning rates) and SoFIE (subatmospheric Exploration Atmospheres)
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA/TM-20210011385; PSI: BASS / BASS-II; NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 (Upward Flame Propagation)

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Flat porous burner emulates solid/liquid material heat of gasification and burning rates via controlled gaseous fuel flow; sustained burning for minutes with zero airflow in elevated-O2 atmospheres; 1g burn rate 3-4x higher than 0g
safety_implication: Shutting down cabin ventilation alone may not immediately extinguish fire in elevated-O2 Exploration Atmospheres; enables rapid non-destructive material flammability screening
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS CIR using ACME Chamber Insert Assembly (CIA) replacing FLEX MDCA while reusing CIR chamber, optics, gas supply, and avionics; 25-50 mm flat porous stainless-steel burner
principal_investigators: James G. Quintiere (PI, Univ. of Maryland); Co-I: Peter B. Sunderland (Univ. of Maryland)
scientific_link_and_applications: Connects gaseous burner physics to solid-fuel flammability from BASS and SoFIE; enables rapid screening of materials in 0g without consuming solid coupons
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: ACME BRE; NASA Task Book / ISS Research Explorer: Burning Rate Emulator (BRE)

key_phenomenon_and_finding: First quasi-steady spherical gaseous diffusion flames; detailed measurement of flame structure, radiative extinction of large flames, and Lewis-number pulsating instabilities (especially in H2)
safety_implication: Provides clean 1D spherical benchmark data to validate 3D CFD fire kinetics, radiation loss, and extinction models for spacecraft fires
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS CIR with ACME CIA housing a small porous spherical burner, radiometers, and cameras (hardware shared with Flame Design and CFI-G)
principal_investigators: Chung K. Law (PI, Princeton Univ.)
scientific_link_and_applications: Directly extends FLEX droplet radiative extinction discoveries from liquid sprays to pure 1D gaseous diffusion flames
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: ACME s-Flames; NASA Task Book / ISS Research Explorer: Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (s-Flame)

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Electric field up to 10 kV drives chemi-ions and charged soot particles to create an ionic wind (electrohydrodynamic force) that reshapes the flame, shifts heat flux, enhances oxidizer mixing, and strongly suppresses soot formation
safety_implication: Potential active, non-chemical flame control, stabilization, and soot-reduction technology for future spacecraft and terrestrial combustors
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS CIR with ACME CIA equipped with coflow jet burner and high-voltage upper mesh electrode (up to 10 kV)
principal_investigators: Derek Dunn-Rankin (PI, UC Irvine)
scientific_link_and_applications: Exploits absence of buoyancy in 0g so weak ionic wind dominates flame aerodynamics and soot precursor residence time
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: ACME E-FIELD Flames; NASA Task Book / ISS Research Explorer: Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Achieved steady non-premixed gaseous cool flames without ozone, plasma, or external preheating using spherical burner configurations
safety_implication: Confirms low-temperature oxidation / cool-flame fire risks exist in gaseous fuel leaks as well as liquid droplet sprays
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS CIR with ACME CIA spherical porous burner operated in high-O2 / inverse diffusion flame mode
principal_investigators: ACME / NASA GRC CFI-G team (extended from FLEX CFI)
scientific_link_and_applications: Directly links FLEX/FLEX-2 liquid droplet cool-flame discoveries to pure gaseous non-premixed flames in ACME
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: ACME CFI-G; ISS Research Explorer: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (CFI-G)

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Full-scale flame spreads slower in large confined volumes than in small lab ducts, delaying smoke generation
safety_implication: Delayed smoke detector activation in large spacecraft habitats; validates scaling from ISS glovebox tests (BASS)
hardware_and_rack_details: Cygnus spacecraft large flow duct after ISS undocking
principal_investigators: David L. Urban / Gary A. Ruff (NASA GRC)
scientific_link_and_applications: Scales up BASS/BASS-II small-duct solid flammability findings to realistic spacecraft habitat dimensions
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: Saffire I-III

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Heat release up to 10 kW did not cause catastrophic cabin overpressure/temp, but released CO, CO2, HF, HCl
safety_implication: Primary threat in large cabins is toxic/acid gas transport; validated prototype smoke eater & CO2 scrubber cleanup
hardware_and_rack_details: Cygnus spacecraft equipped with fire-cleanup/scrubber diagnostics and gas sensors
principal_investigators: David L. Urban / Gary A. Ruff (NASA GRC)
scientific_link_and_applications: Integrates fire growth scaling with post-fire toxic gas remediation
official_identifiers_and_publications: NTRS 20210011521; NASA PSI: Saffire IV-V

fuel.material: Teflon, Kapton, Pyrell foam, cellulose, silicone rubber, DBP

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Microgravity smoke particle size distribution differs from 1g (aging 10-1800 s); compared Shuttle ionization vs ISS photoelectric sensors
safety_implication: Single-moment smoke sensors struggle with tiny Teflon/Kapton particles vs dust; drives multi-wavelength/multi-moment detectors
hardware_and_rack_details: MSG (Microgravity Science Glovebox) aerosol measurement duct
principal_investigators: David L. Urban / Marit E. Meyer (NASA GRC)
scientific_link_and_applications: Complements BASS/Saffire by characterizing microgravity smoke particle morphology for spacecraft fire detection
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: SAME; DOI 10.1016/j.firesaf.2018.04.004

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Measures how internal solid fuel heating/temperature shifts flame growth and extinction limits in microgravity
safety_implication: Defines critical thermal thickness and preheating risk near hot spacecraft electronics/heaters
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS CIR equipped with SoFIE (Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction) insert replacing ACME CIA
principal_investigators: Paul V. Ferkul / NASA GRC SoFIE team
scientific_link_and_applications: Follow-on to BASS and ACME inside CIR, moving from gaseous emulation (ACME BRE) back to thick solid fuels under variable pressure/O2
source_id: NASA ISS Research Explorer / Daily Summary
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA ISS Research Explorer: SoFIE-GEL

fuel.material: black cast PMMA rods (+ 0-3.3 kW/m2 radiant flux)

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Blue bubble flames and two extinction limits (spread LOC-FS & regression LOC-FR); significantly lower LOC in 0g than 1g
safety_implication: Proves Earth flammability screening is non-conservative for subatmospheric Exploration Atmospheres
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS CIR / SoFIE cylindrical flow tunnel with external radiant heaters
principal_investigators: Fletcher J. Miller / NASA GRC SoFIE team
scientific_link_and_applications: Directly extends BASS low-flow 0g solid flammability findings to subatmospheric Exploration Atmospheres (56.5 kPa / 34% O2)
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA Task Book: SoFIE-MIST; ICES-2023-133

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Baseline 1g Earth certification standard where upward natural convection (~20-30 cm/s) dominates flame spread
safety_implication: Historically assumed to be worst-case, but BASS and SoFIE proved 0g low-flow regimes can ignite at lower O2
hardware_and_rack_details: 1g vertical combustion test chamber
principal_investigators: NASA
scientific_link_and_applications: Reference baseline challenged by BASS/BASS-II U-shaped flammability curve and SoFIE-MIST subatmospheric tests
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Sea-level pressure and O2 in microgravity; HVAC airflow creates critical low-velocity regime matching BASS peak flammability
safety_implication: Requires strict material limits, ventilation shutoff protocols, and photoelectric smoke detection
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS habitable modules (0g, forced HVAC ventilation)
principal_investigators: NASA
scientific_link_and_applications: Target operating regime evaluated by BASS/BASS-II, SAME, and ACME
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA ISS Environmental Control Reference

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Recommended by EAWG (8.2 psia / 34% O2) to minimize EVA prebreathe time while balancing hypoxia and fire risk
safety_implication: Significantly increases material flammability; primary target environment for SoFIE and ACME BRE validation
hardware_and_rack_details: Future Artemis/Gateway/Lunar surface pressurized habitats
principal_investigators: NASA EAWG
scientific_link_and_applications: Primary target regime driving ACME BRE and SoFIE testing
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA Exploration Atmospheres Working Group (EAWG) Report

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Demonstrated soot-free quasi-steady spherical diffusion flames by tailoring stoichiometric mixture fraction (Zst) via fuel-side vs oxidizer-side inert dilution: diluting fuel / enriching oxidizer (high Zst) shifts flame sheet toward fuel side, cooling/thinning the fuel-rich pyrolysis zone to eliminate soot; diluting oxidizer (low Zst) increases soot and radiation loss leading to radiative extinction
safety_implication: Enables rational design of soot-free, clean-burning spacecraft and terrestrial combustors and validates radiation/soot-inception models
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS CIR with ACME CIA spherical porous burner (normal and inverse injection capability)
principal_investigators: Richard L. Axelbaum (PI, Washington Univ. in St. Louis)
scientific_link_and_applications: Builds on FLEX radiative extinction physics and pairs with s-Flame to decouple soot formation, radiation loss, and Zst effects without buoyancy
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: ACME Flame Design; NASA Task Book / ISS Research Explorer: Flame Design

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Provides steady, flicker-free axisymmetric coflow laminar diffusion flames in 0g up to elevated pressures to isolate soot growth and radiative heat transfer from buoyancy
safety_implication: Supplies high-fidelity validation benchmarks for 2D/3D CFD soot and radiation models used in spacecraft and terrestrial combustion
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS CIR with ACME CIA axisymmetric coflow laminar jet burner and optical soot/temperature diagnostics
principal_investigators: Marshall B. Long (PI, Yale Univ.); Co-I: Mitchell D. Smooke (Yale Univ.)
scientific_link_and_applications: Part of the 6-experiment ACME suite complementing Flame Design and E-FIELD Flames on soot formation in microgravity
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: ACME CLD Flame; NASA Task Book / ISS Research Explorer: Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (CLD Flame)

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Investigated flame spread along linear and lattice arrays of liquid fuel droplets rather than isolated/twin droplets; revealed group combustion regimes, inter-droplet heat/vapor transfer, and percolation limits for flame spread
safety_implication: Models real fuel-spray and mist fire propagation and extinction limits in microgravity spacecraft and spray combustors
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS CIR / MDCA hardware adapted for multi-droplet linear/lattice array generation and sequential ignition
principal_investigators: Masato Mikami (PI, Yamaguchi Univ., JAXA)
scientific_link_and_applications: Extends FLEX-1 (single droplets) and FLEX-2 (multi-component/twin droplets) to multi-droplet array group combustion and spray flame spread
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: FLEX-2J; JAXA Group Combustion / Droplet Array Experiment

fuel.material: H2, CH4, C2H4, propane, n-butane, n-pentane

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Six-experiment suite (BRE, Flame Design, s-Flame, E-FIELD Flames, CLD Flame, CFI-G) studying: (1) spacecraft fire prevention & solid-material emulation (BRE), (2) soot-free flames & Zst control (Flame Design), (3) radiative extinction & instabilities (s-Flame), (4) active electric-field soot/flame control (E-FIELD), (5) elevated-pressure soot CFD benchmarks (CLD), and (6) gaseous cool flames (CFI-G)
safety_implication: Unified gaseous microgravity testbed bridging fundamental combustion physics, soot reduction, CFD validation, and spacecraft fire safety
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS Destiny Lab CIR rack using modular ACME Chamber Insert Assembly (CIA) that replaced FLEX MDCA while reusing CIR chamber, optical diagnostics, gas mixing, and avionics
principal_investigators: Dennis P. Stocker (NASA GRC Project Scientist); PIs: James G. Quintiere (BRE), Richard L. Axelbaum (Flame Design), Chung K. Law (s-Flame), Derek Dunn-Rankin (E-FIELD Flames), Marshall B. Long (CLD Flame), Forman A. Williams / NASA GRC (CFI-G)
scientific_link_and_applications: Direct hardware and scientific successor to FLEX inside CIR (radiative extinction & cool flames -> gas phase) and gas-phase counterpart to BASS solid-fuel flammability studies
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: ACME; ISS Research Explorer: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME)

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Fourth investigation in the ISS FLEX suite studying isolated single-droplet combustion of renewable alcohol/alkane biofuel surrogates (heptane/ethanol, decane/1-hexanol) in microgravity; quantified preferential vaporization, soot shell dynamics, and radiative/diffusive extinction limits without buoyancy
safety_implication: Provides validated surrogate chemical-kinetic and evaporation benchmarks for next-generation low-soot aviation/biofuel blends and spacecraft fluid fire hazards
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS Destiny Lab CIR rack with MDCA chamber insert, multi-fuel syringe dispensing needles, and high-speed backlit/flame imaging diagnostics
principal_investigators: Patrizio Massoli (PI, CNR-Istituto Motori, Italy); PS: Daniel L. Dietrich (NASA GRC)
scientific_link_and_applications: Completes the four-part ISS FLEX droplet campaign (FLEX, FLEX-2/CFI, FLEX-2J, FLEX-ICE-GA), bridging single alkanes to oxygenated biofuel blends
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: FLEX-ICE-GA; NASA Technical Fact Sheet: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) / Italian Combustion Experiment for Green Air

fuel.material: 10 flame-retardant (FR) treated textiles (cotton, cotton/nylon, Nomex blends)

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Evaluated self-extinguishment and flame spread of 10 commercial flame-retardant textiles under forced low-speed ventilation in 0g versus 1g upward-burn standards; demonstrated how fabric weave density, char formation, and low convective cooling alter flame persistence in microgravity
safety_implication: Directly benchmarks commercial fire-resistant fabrics for crew clothing and habitat interiors where 1g upward-burn screening can mispredict 0g ventilation-driven burning
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) using the SPICE fan-driven small wind-tunnel flow duct and fabric sample frames
principal_investigators: Milliken & Company Research Team; NASA GRC BASS/MSG Team (Sandra L. Olson, Paul V. Ferkul)
scientific_link_and_applications: Commercial/applied extension of BASS and BASS-II translating fundamental microgravity solid flammability limits into textile fire-safety engineering
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: BASS-M; ISS Research Explorer: Burning and Suppression of Solids - Milliken (BASS-M)

key_phenomenon_and_finding: Precursor investigation to ACME CLD Flame conducted in MSG/SPICE; characterized lifted laminar jet diffusion flames, flame stabilization heights, and blow-off/dilution limits in 0g where diluted weak flames remain stable at much lower fuel concentrations than in 1g
safety_implication: Establishes baseline stabilization and dilution blowout limits for gaseous fuel leaks in ventilated spacecraft compartments prior to ACME CIR operations
hardware_and_rack_details: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with SPICE coflow wind-tunnel duct and laminar gas-jet nozzle
principal_investigators: Marshall B. Long (PI, Yale Univ.); Co-I: Mitchell D. Smooke (Yale Univ.)
scientific_link_and_applications: Direct pathfinder experiment for ACME Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (CLD Flame), linking MSG/SPICE diagnostics to ISS CIR ACME hardware
official_identifiers_and_publications: NASA PSI: SLICE; ISS Research Explorer: Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment (SLICE)
